name: ClipVault
description:
A clipboard history (Super+V) that pops up right where you type, with a private vault for notes and accounts.

• Opens right under the text cursor and pastes into the field you were typing in
• Text and image history with search, pinned items and tooltips
• Notes and accounts (Super+Shift+V); passwords are stored in the GNOME Keyring
• Password generator (Super+Alt+P) with configurable rules
• Private mode and automatic clearing of copied passwords

Clipboard access: ClipVault reads the clipboard to record what you copy (text and images) and writes to it when you pick an item, a note or a password so it can be pasted. Nothing is recorded in private mode or when a password manager marks the content as secret.

While enabled, ClipVault takes over Super+V from GNOME's notification list shortcut and restores it when disabled (this can be turned off in the preferences). Clipboard history is stored locally in ~/.local/share/clipvault and never leaves your computer.
